Just as the title suggests; wondering if there's a way to override it. From what I understand, userscripts modify all existing code on the site after it's done rendering in the browser. So I'm curious as to whether it's even *possible*. I know that `@import url(https://voat.co/Content/[Light/Dark]);` works to force whatever underlying default theme is used, but this seems to have no effect on AVE (and its modification of the CSS according to its preset).

So if AVE is set to dark-mode and I force light-mode through the subverse's CSS, then certain elements (such as highlighting) will still render in dark-mode, as per AVE. It's not the end of the world, but just curious if someone's figured out a way around this, is all.
Does anyone know if there's a way to force AVE to switch to either light or dark mode?

Nevermind, I figured it out myself; for anyone that's interested in this, basically: if you set the background image of any element to anything, it'll bypass AVE's automatic coloration of whatever it happens to be (post highlighting, background colors, etc).

So if you just want something to remain transparent (or whatever color you want) and not have it be toggled to a dark color after someone switches to dark-mode, when your theme is meant to run in light-mode (or vice-versa): simply make an image that is one single pixel tall/wide, and set it to whatever color (or transparency) you want. Make that image the background picture for said element.

Just tested it and it works like a charm. Enjoy.
